title: Cyberattack Disrupts Hundreds of French Supermarkets
paragraphs: A major cyberattack has disrupted hundreds of supermarkets across France, forcing many stores to throw away large quantities of fresh and frozen food after hackers targeted the systems that control their refrigerators.

The attack took place overnight on October 11 to 12, 2026, and it affected several of France's biggest supermarket chains, including Intermarché, Netto, Coopérative U, Carrefour and Monoprix. According to Roland Lescure, France's finance minister, around 700 of the country's 10,000 supermarkets were affected.

The hackers took control of the refrigeration management systems used by the stores. As a result, refrigerators and freezers stopped working properly, and in some cases, temperatures reportedly reached as high as 50 degrees Celsius. With their fresh and frozen products spoiled, many stores had no choice but to discard them. There were also reports of fires breaking out in several stores.

The impact varied between chains. Groupement Mousquetaires, which operates the Intermarché and Netto chains, said that 300 of its stores had been affected, and that some refrigerated and frozen display cases were still out of service several days later. Meanwhile, Coopérative U said that 80 of its 2,000 stores had been hit. Its chief executive, Dominique Schelcher, described the incident as an attack on the French food supply chain.

The refrigeration management software had been supplied by Danfoss, a Danish company. According to Danfoss, most of the affected systems were older products that no longer received software or security updates. The company advised its customers to keep their systems updated with the latest software and to protect them with a firewall.
Lescure insisted that there was no risk to France's food supply. However, he acknowledged that the attack touched the heart of the country's food security.

The Paris prosecutor's office has launched an investigation into the large-scale cyberattack through its cybercrime unit, and it is examining the extent of the damage caused by the spoiled food and the fires. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has also asked ANSSI, France's national cybersecurity agency, to investigate. So far, the attackers have not been identified.
The incident has raised concerns about the security of the many connected devices that businesses now depend on, especially older equipment that no longer receives updates.
